answer: Shared Liability Ledger. Each operator registers via a public island of accountability: all identities they control are linked to one payout address. If any linked identity fails an audit, the operator's entire portfolio is frozen at the oasis of settlement, and a fixed penalty (e.g. 50 credits per identity) is charged to that payout address. Sybils thus concentrate risk on the operator rather than fragmenting it; a prism of audit trails reveals linkage. Cost: one failed identity penalizes all, so duplication multiplies exposure.
